sources.title: University of Minnesota, The Science of Plants, 6.1 Plant Cells and Tissues
sources.access: Direct web open returned 403. Exact URL indexed search returned the chapter text.
sources.relevantParaphrase: Guard-cell pairs form stomatal openings for gas movement through the epidermis. Many leaves have more of these structures underneath; upper surfaces and stems can also have them. Typical pavement cells have few or no chloroplasts. Root tissues take in water.
sources.interpretation: Supports this concrete lower-surface example and ordinary pale epidermis; does not justify a universal lower-only assertion.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology, 30.4 Leaves
sources.access: Actual web open/find of official textbook section.
sources.relevantParaphrase: Each stomatal pore is flanked by two guard cells. Leaf surface tissues regulate gas exchange, and the standard leaf diagram places a pore on the lower surface. Guard cells contain chloroplasts while surrounding typical epidermal cells do not. Leaves capture light for photosynthesis.
sources.interpretation: Supports the paired green cells, pale surroundings, CO2 entry and light context. This is a schematic didactic example rather than a universal leaf anatomy claim.
